title: Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage — Hospital Days Already Reversed Within an Uncertified Lapse
content:
**Rule (Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage).** A day already reversed as a hospital day on the lapse's block is not a day the uncertified lapse reverses: the days of the hospital-day reversal that lie inside the reversal's span come off the lapse's days before the supplemental effective date, all of that overlap when its last day falls before the date, the overlap from its first day up to the day before the date when the date falls after its first day and on or before its last, and none otherwise or when there is no such record.

The lapse is the uncertified-day reversal posted against the booked-days entry of the coverage's latest booked coinsurance block after the resident's original coinsurance charge for that block was posted; the lapse's block is that block. The hospital-day reversal is the reversal with the reason hospital day posted against the same booked-days entry; only its days that lie inside the lapse's span are considered. What changes is the count of the lapse's reversed days before the supplemental effective date for the reduction for reversed covered days.

### Basis Q&A

**The date falls after the last overlapping hospital day — what comes off?** Every hospital-day reversed day inside the span.

**The date falls after the first overlapping day and on or before the last?** Those days from the first up to the day before the date.

**Any other case, or no hospital-day reversal on the block?** Nothing comes off.

*Hypothetical worked example:* the lapse spans the 22nd to the 28th, and a hospital-day reversal on the same entry covers the 24th and 25th. With a supplemental effective date of the 25th, one day (the 24th) comes off; with the 29th, two days; with the 23rd, none.
